isoforms.description: Alternative isoform with 13 additional residues at N-terminus; neuron-specific; reduced AXIN1 binding affinity

prosite_patterns.name: Protein kinases ATP-binding region signature
prosite_patterns.description: ATP binding pocket with hinge residues Asp133, Val135; conserved Lys85 coordinates ATP phosphates

prosite_patterns.name: Serine/Threonine protein kinases active-site signature
prosite_patterns.description: Contains HRD catalytic motif essential for phosphotransfer

signaling_motifs.description: N-terminal inhibitory phosphorylation site; phosphorylated by Akt/PKB/PKA causing ~200-fold decrease in kcat/KM toward pS45-beta-catenin; pseudosubstrate mechanism occupying primed substrate binding pocket formed by R96-R180-K205

Activating autophosphorylation site in activation loop; essential for catalytic activity (~5-fold activation); Y216F mutation nearly abolishes activity; pY216 phosphate interacts with R220 and R223; pY216 constitutively present in cells; phosphorylation flips tyrosine out of substrate binding groove stabilizing active conformation
Glycine-rich P-loop (phosphate-binding loop) for ATP binding; interacts with ATP beta-phosphate; highly flexible loop between beta-strand and alpha-helix

P+4 priming phosphate binding pocket formed by Arg96, Arg180, Lys205; recognizes phospho-Ser/Thr at position +4 in substrates (S/T-X-X-X-pS/pT consensus); unique GSK3 specificity determinant enabling >1000-fold enhancement of primed vs unprimed substrate phosphorylation; structural basis for priming requirement
Catalytic loop containing conserved His-Arg-Asp motif essential for phosphotransfer; Asp181 (D) coordinates Mg2+ ion; Arg180 (R) also part of priming phosphate binding pocket

Activation loop (residues 200-226); well-ordered and positioned against alpha-helical domain even without phosphorylation; DFG motif (Asp200-Phe201-Gly202) coordinates ATP-Mg2+; contains Tyr216 phosphorylation site; orientation similar to activated kinases enabling constitutive activity; positioned to open substrate binding groove
Hinge region connecting N-terminal and C-terminal lobes; Asp133 and Val135 form H-bonds with ATP/inhibitors; critical for ATP/ADP binding and catalysis; targeted by ATP-competitive inhibitors

AXIN1 binding channel formed by alpha-helix (residues 262-273) and extended loop (285-299); hydrophobic groove formed by Val263, Leu266, Val267, Ile270 packs with AXIN1 hydrophobic ridge (Phe388, Leu392, Leu396, Val399); critical for destruction complex assembly; enables >20,000-fold catalytic enhancement
Regulatory helix (residues 96-104); contains Arg96 of priming phosphate binding pocket; critical for substrate binding and maintaining active kinase conformation; important for allosteric regulation
N-terminal beta-strand domain; smaller lobe containing P-loop, alphaC-helix, and ATP binding pocket; houses Lys85 that coordinates ATP phosphates
C-terminal alpha-helical domain; larger lobe containing catalytic machinery, activation loop, and substrate binding groove; forms most of enzyme core

experimental_structures.description: GSK3beta in catalytically active conformation without activation-segment phosphorylation; sulphonate ion mimicking phosphate group bridges activation segment and N-terminal domain; demonstrates constitutively active conformation

GSK-3β complexed with AMP-PNP (non-hydrolyzable ATP analog); Mg2+ octahedrally coordinated; shows ATP binding mode and active site architecture; homo-dimer with C2 symmetry; widely used reference structure for ATP binding

GSK3β in complex with FRATtide peptide inhibitor; sulfate ion adjacent to Val214 represents binding site for phosphoserine on primed substrates; demonstrates priming mechanism and how pseudo-substrate inhibitors work

Highest resolution structure of GSK3β; activation loop positioned in active conformation similar to phosphorylated kinases (CDK2, ERK2); demonstrates unphosphorylated GSK3β adopts constitutively active conformation; activation loop orientation enables substrate binding without requiring pTyr216
Crystal structure of human GSK3β in complex with ATP-competitive inhibitor showing inhibitor binding mode in ATP pocket
Unphosphorylated GSK-3β structure showing phosphate binding site architecture; PO4 ion in position mimicking substrate phosphate; activation loop well-ordered
High-resolution GSK-3β in complex with imidazo[1,5-a]pyridine-3-carboxamide inhibitor 16 showing detailed inhibitor-protein interactions

alphafold_prediction.confidence_summary: High confidence (pLDDT > 90) for structured kinase domain core (residues ~56-343 encompassing N-terminal and C-terminal lobes); moderate to high confidence (pLDDT 70-90) for N-terminal regulatory region (residues 1-55); lower confidence (pLDDT 50-70) for C-terminal tail (residues 344-420) indicating intrinsic disorder or flexibility; activation loop well-predicted with high confidence

post_translational_modifications.function: Inhibitory - causes ~200-fold decrease in kcat/KM toward primed substrates; creates pseudo-substrate that blocks primed substrate binding pocket
post_translational_modifications.description: Phosphorylation by Akt upon insulin/growth factor signaling. pSer9 occupies R96-R180-K205 priming phosphate binding pocket, preventing primed substrate access. With pS9-GSK3B, KM toward pS45-beta-catenin ≥2 μM with no saturation vs KM=0.27 μM for unphosphorylated GSK3B:AXIN complex. Major regulatory input from PI3K/Akt pathway.

post_translational_modifications.function: Activating - essential for kinase activity (~5-fold enhancement); phosphate interacts with R220 and R223 stabilizing activation loop
post_translational_modifications.description: Autophosphorylation in trans within activation loop (residues 200-226). Y216F mutation nearly abolishes kinase activity indicating essential role. pY216 flipped out of substrate binding groove, with phosphate making ionic interactions with Arg220 and Arg223. Constitutively phosphorylated in cells; represents majority of cellular GSK3β pool. Located in activation loop which adopts active conformation even without phosphorylation, but pY216 further stabilizes and enhances activity.
Alternative inhibitory phosphorylation site in C-terminal region; mechanism distinct from Ser9

post_translational_modifications.function: Regulatory - controls function independent of phosphorylation state
post_translational_modifications.description: S-nitrosylation of cysteine residues regulates GSK3β activity independently of Ser9/Tyr216 phosphorylation state; redox-sensitive regulation
Ubiquitination targets GSK3β for proteasomal degradation; regulated by SCF-FBXW7α E3 ligase; affects protein stability and cellular levels
Lysine acetylation regulates activity; deacetylase SIRT2 modulates GSK3 isoforms independent of inhibitory phosphorylation
Palmitoylation by ZDHHC4 directs membrane localization; affects subcellular distribution and substrate access
ADP-ribosylation by PARP10 modulates kinase activity

function.uniprot_function: Constitutively active protein kinase that acts as negative regulator in hormonal control of glucose homeostasis, Wnt signaling and regulation of transcription factors and microtubules. Involved in energy metabolism, neuronal cell development, and body pattern formation. Phosphorylates and inactivates glycogen synthase (GYS1 and GYS2) contributing to insulin regulation of glycogen synthesis. In Wnt signaling, forms multimeric destruction complex with APC, AXIN1 and CTNNB1/beta-catenin, phosphorylating beta-catenin at Ser33, Ser37, Thr41 (after CK1α priming at Ser45) leading to beta-TrCP-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. Phosphorylates tau protein (MAPT) at multiple sites decreasing microtubule binding ability; tau hyperphosphorylation is principal component of neurofibrillary tangles in Alzheimer disease. Regulates circadian clock via phosphorylation of ARNTL/BMAL1 and CLOCK proteins. Phosphorylates c-Myc (Thr58), cyclin D1 (Thr286), c-Jun, CREB targeting them for degradation and regulating cell cycle and transcription. Exhibits processivity: after priming phosphorylation, sequentially phosphorylates substrates from C-terminus to N-terminus at S/T-X-X-X-pS/pT consensus sites.
function.catalytic_activity: ATP + [protein]-L-serine = ADP + [protein]-L-serine phosphate; ATP + [protein]-L-threonine = ADP + [protein]-L-threonine phosphate (EC 2.7.11.26)
function.substrate_specificity: Requires priming phosphorylation at position +4 relative to target site (consensus: S/T-X-X-X-pS/pT where pS/pT is phosphoserine or phosphothreonine). Priming enhances phosphorylation >1000-fold. Arg96, Arg180, Lys205 form specific pocket recognizing priming phosphate. Exhibits processivity: after initial priming, phosphorylates substrates sequentially from C-terminus to N-terminus creating multiple phosphorylation sites. Key substrates: CTNNB1/beta-catenin (Ser33, Ser37, Thr41 after CK1α primes Ser45); GYS1/glycogen synthase (Ser640, 644, 648, 652 sequential); MAPT/tau (>40 sites including Thr231, Ser235, Ser396, Ser404); c-Myc (Thr58 after Ser62 priming); cyclin D1 (Thr286); c-Jun; CREB; IRF1 (Thr181). Some substrates are non-primed but these are minority.
subcellular_location: Nucleus (accumulates upon amino acid starvation; shuttles between cytoplasm and nucleus; higher activity when nuclear)
Mitochondrion (localizes under ischemia/reperfusion stress; higher activity)
function.tissue_specificity: Ubiquitously expressed with particularly high levels in brain (especially neurons; brain-enriched compared to GSK3A), testis, skeletal muscle, liver, adipose tissue, heart, kidney. Both GSK3A and GSK3B show tissue-dependent differential expression patterns. Elevated expression in skeletal muscle of type 2 diabetes patients.

biological_process.term: negative regulation of glycogen biosynthetic process

binding_details.interface: AXIN1 C-terminal region (aa ~383-410) binds GSK3B scaffold binding region (aa 260-300); amphipathic alpha-helix of AXIN1 (Phe388, Leu392, Leu396, Val399) packs into hydrophobic channel of GSK3B (Val263, Leu266, Val267, Ile270)
binding_details.functional_effect: AXIN1 scaffold brings GSK3B and beta-catenin into proximity; enhances beta-catenin phosphorylation >20,000-fold by decreasing KM ~20-fold (from >2 μM to 0.27 μM) and increasing kcat; drives catalytic cycle of beta-catenin destruction; GSK3B phosphorylates AXIN1 at Ser322/326/330 increasing AXIN1 stability and at Thr485/Ser490/Ser497 increasing AXIN1-beta-catenin interaction
binding_details.stoichiometry: 1:1 binding; AXIN1 is rate-limiting component in destruction complex (~1000-fold lower cellular concentration than GSK3B, beta-catenin, APC)

binding_details.interface: Similar to AXIN1; scaffold bringing GSK3B and CTNNB1 together in destruction complex
binding_details.functional_effect: Enhances beta-catenin phosphorylation >20,000-fold; functionally redundant with AXIN1; AXIN2 is Wnt target gene providing negative feedback

binding_details.interface: Part of destruction complex; APC binds both AXIN and beta-catenin; exact APC-GSK3B interface less characterized than AXIN-GSK3B; interaction likely AXIN-mediated
binding_details.functional_effect: Scaffolds beta-catenin degradation complex cooperating with AXIN; provides multiple beta-catenin binding sites; APC truncation mutations (>80% of colorectal cancers) disrupt destruction complex assembly despite normal GSK3B activity, preventing beta-catenin degradation and driving tumorigenesis

binding_details.interface: Substrate binding at kinase active site; N-terminal region of beta-catenin containing Ser33/37, Thr41 sites docks in substrate binding groove; requires AXIN scaffold for efficient phosphorylation
binding_details.functional_effect: Sequential phosphorylation: CK1α phosphorylates Ser45 (priming); GSK3B then phosphorylates Thr41, Ser37, Ser33 in C-to-N direction (processivity); pSer33 and pSer37 create DSGXXS motif recognized by beta-TrCP E3 ubiquitin ligase leading to ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation; KM without AXIN scaffold ≥2 μM; KM with AXIN = 0.27 μM (>20,000-fold kcat/KM enhancement)

binding_details.interface: Both kinases co-localize in destruction complex through AXIN binding; no direct GSK3B-CK1 interaction characterized
binding_details.functional_effect: CK1α primes beta-catenin at Ser45 (and other substrates) enabling GSK3B phosphorylation at Ser33/37/Thr41; sequential two-kinase mechanism; both kinases remain active in destruction complex upon Wnt stimulation but substrate access is blocked; CK1 phosphorylation at Ser45 increases Ser33/37/Thr41 phosphorylation by GSK3B >1000-fold demonstrating critical priming requirement

binding_details.interface: Akt phosphorylates GSK3B at Ser9; may involve transient complex formation
binding_details.functional_effect: Akt activated by insulin/growth factors via PI3K pathway phosphorylates GSK3B Ser9 causing ~200-fold decrease in activity toward primed substrates (KM increases from 0.27 μM to ≥2 μM with no saturation); pSer9 acts as pseudo-substrate blocking priming phosphate binding pocket (R96-R180-K205); enables insulin/growth factor control of glycogen synthesis, protein synthesis (via glycogen synthase, eIF2B), and cell survival (via beta-catenin, Myc stabilization)

binding_details.interface: Multiple phosphorylation sites on tau protein (>40 potential GSK3B sites throughout tau sequence)
binding_details.functional_effect: Major tau kinase in brain; hyperphosphorylation reduces tau's ability to bind and stabilize microtubules by ~90%; hyperphosphorylated tau aggregates into paired helical filaments forming neurofibrillary tangles, a pathological hallmark of Alzheimer disease; some tau sites are primed, others are non-primed substrates; contributes to tau pathology in AD, FTD, other tauopathies

binding_details.interface: GSK3B phosphorylates c-Myc N-terminal transactivation domain (Myc box I)
binding_details.functional_effect: Phosphorylation at Thr58 (after Ser62 priming) creates phosphodegron recognized by FBW7 E3 ubiquitin ligase targeting c-Myc for ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation (t1/2 ~20-30 min); regulates cell proliferation, growth, and transformation; GSK3B acts as tumor suppressor by limiting c-Myc protein levels

binding_details.interface: DVL binds to AXIN in destruction complex upon Wnt receptor activation; disrupts AXIN-GSK3B-beta-catenin complex geometry
binding_details.functional_effect: Upon Wnt ligand binding to Frizzled receptor, DVL recruited to plasma membrane and binds AXIN; disrupts destruction complex activity toward beta-catenin despite GSK3B remaining active and bound; mechanism involves altered substrate presentation rather than GSK3B inhibition; enables beta-catenin stabilization and Wnt pathway activation

binding_details.interface: beta-TrCP recognizes pSer33/pSer37 motif (DSGXXS) in GSK3B-phosphorylated beta-catenin; no direct GSK3B-BTRC interaction
binding_details.functional_effect: beta-TrCP is F-box component of SCF E3 ubiquitin ligase complex; recognizes beta-catenin only after GSK3B phosphorylation creates recognition degron; ubiquitinates beta-catenin leading to proteasomal degradation; completes beta-catenin destruction pathway initiated by GSK3B phosphorylation

binding_details.interface: GSK3B phosphorylates C-terminal region of glycogen synthase containing regulatory phosphorylation sites
binding_details.functional_effect: Sequential phosphorylation in C-to-N direction (processivity); each site primes next; phosphorylation inhibits glycogen synthase activity reducing glycogen synthesis; originally identified substrate giving GSK3 its name; insulin signaling inhibits GSK3B (via Akt pSer9) relieving inhibition of glycogen synthase and promoting glycogen synthesis; critical for glucose homeostasis

key_binding_partners: AXIN1 (scaffold, Kd=35 µM, >20,000-fold kcat/KM enhancement, rate-limiting)
APC (scaffold, truncation in 80% CRC abolishes destruction complex)
CTNNB1/beta-catenin (substrate, Km=0.27 µM with AXIN, sites: Ser33/37/Thr41)
CSNK1A1/CK1α (priming kinase for beta-catenin Ser45, >1000-fold priming effect)
AKT1 (upstream inhibitory kinase, pSer9 causes ~200-fold activity decrease)
MAPT/tau (substrate, >40 sites, neurofibrillary tangles in AD)
c-Myc (substrate, Thr58 after Ser62 priming, t1/2=20-30 min)
Cyclin D1 (substrate, Thr286, cell cycle regulation)
DVL1/2/3 (Wnt pathway, disrupts destruction complex geometry)
summary.destruction_complex_stoichiometry: AXIN:APC:GSK3B:CK1:CTNNB1 forms dynamic complex. AXIN is rate-limiting scaffold with cellular concentration ~1000-fold lower than GSK3B, beta-catenin, or APC. APC binds multiple AXIN and beta-catenin molecules. Single AXIN molecule is expected to bind one copy each of GSK3B, CK1α, and beta-catenin. Complex undergoes catalytic cycles: beta-catenin binding, sequential phosphorylation by CK1 then GSK3B, beta-TrCP recruitment, ubiquitination, release.

substrate_beta_catenin_free_enzyme.conditions: In vitro steady-state kinetics without AXIN scaffold; physiologically irrelevant
substrate_beta_catenin_free_enzyme.notes: Free GSK3B has very poor activity toward beta-catenin; does not saturate even at high [substrate]; demonstrates absolute requirement for AXIN scaffold for physiologically relevant beta-catenin phosphorylation

substrate_beta_catenin_axin_complex.conditions: AXIN scaffold present; physiologically relevant form in destruction complex
substrate_beta_catenin_axin_complex.reference: Gavagan et al. eLife 2023; doi:10.7554/eLife.85444; PMID: 36594429
substrate_beta_catenin_axin_complex.notes: AXIN scaffold decreases KM ~20-fold (from >2 µM to 0.27 µM) and increases kcat, resulting in >20,000-fold kcat/KM enhancement. One of most dramatic scaffold effects known in cell signaling. AXIN brings enzyme and substrate into proximity and optimally positions substrate. Demonstrates scaffolds can convert essentially inactive enzyme-substrate pair into highly efficient catalytic system. Critical for understanding destruction complex mechanism.

substrate_beta_catenin_ps9_inhibited.conditions: Ser9 phosphorylated by Akt (insulin/growth factor signaling active)
substrate_beta_catenin_ps9_inhibited.notes: pS9 phosphorylation causes ~200-fold decrease in kcat/KM toward primed substrates. Enzyme does not saturate at high [substrate] (KM ≥2 µM, likely much higher). Mechanism: pSer9 occupies priming phosphate binding pocket (R96-R180-K205) acting as pseudo-substrate, preventing primed substrate access. AXIN scaffold partially protects against Ser9 inhibition (7-fold increase in KM for PKA phosphorylation of Ser9 when AXIN bound). Major regulatory mechanism linking growth factor/insulin signaling to beta-catenin and glycogen metabolism.

autophosphorylation_tyr216.mechanism: Autophosphorylation in trans between GSK3B molecules
autophosphorylation_tyr216.notes: Autophosphorylation in trans; constitutively phosphorylated in cells representing majority of GSK3B pool. ~5-fold increase in activity. Y216F mutation reduces activity to <10% of wild-type, nearly abolishing kinase function. pY216 phosphate makes ionic interactions with R220 and R223 in activation loop stabilizing active conformation. pTyr216 flipped out of substrate binding groove. Even unphosphorylated GSK3B has active conformation but pY216 further enhances and stabilizes activity.

substrate_glycogen_synthase.processivity: Sequential C-to-N phosphorylation after initial priming
substrate_glycogen_synthase.notes: Original substrate giving GSK3 its name. Sequential phosphorylation in C-terminal to N-terminal direction with each site priming next (processivity). Phosphorylation inhibits glycogen synthase activity reducing glycogen synthesis. Insulin/growth factor signaling inhibits GSK3B via Akt pSer9, relieving glycogen synthase inhibition and promoting glycogen synthesis. Critical for glucose homeostasis and insulin sensitivity.

substrate_tau_protein.priming_requirement: Some sites require priming, others are non-primed
substrate_tau_protein.notes: Major tau kinase in brain. Hyperphosphorylation at multiple sites (>40 potential GSK3B sites identified) reduces tau's microtubule-binding ability by ~90%. Hyperphosphorylated tau detaches from microtubules and aggregates into paired helical filaments forming neurofibrillary tangles, pathological hallmark of Alzheimer disease. Some tau sites follow canonical S/T-X-X-X-pS/pT priming requirement, others are non-primed substrates. Contributes to tau pathology in AD, frontotemporal dementia, and other tauopathies.

substrate_c_myc.notes: Phosphorylation at Thr58 (after Ser62 priming by ERK/CDK) creates phosphodegron (DSG-X-X-pS motif) recognized by FBW7 E3 ubiquitin ligase. Ubiquitination targets c-Myc for proteasomal degradation (half-life 20-30 minutes). Regulates cell proliferation, growth, metabolism, and transformation. GSK3B acts as tumor suppressor by limiting c-Myc protein levels. Loss of GSK3B regulation (e.g., via aberrant Wnt signaling) stabilizes c-Myc contributing to oncogenesis.

akt_phosphorylation_of_gsk3b_ser9.fold_change_with_axin: 7-fold decrease in kcat/KM when AXIN scaffold present
akt_phosphorylation_of_gsk3b_ser9.notes: AXIN scaffold partially protects GSK3B from Ser9 phosphorylation by Akt: 7-fold drop in kcat/KM for PKA phosphorylation primarily from 4-fold increase in KM. Suggests AXIN binding alters Ser9 accessibility. Provides mechanism for differential regulation of scaffold-bound vs free GSK3B pools.

reactome.pathway_name: Degradation of beta-catenin by the destruction complex
TCF dependent signaling in response to WNT

pathways.pathway_role_summary: GSK3B is master negative regulator kinase integrating multiple signaling inputs. In Wnt/beta-catenin pathway, GSK3B phosphorylates beta-catenin (Ser33/37/Thr41 after CK1α primes Ser45) as part of destruction complex with AXIN1/2 and APC. AXIN scaffold provides >20,000-fold catalytic enhancement (KM decrease from >2 μM to 0.27 μM plus kcat increase), making scaffold-dependent vs scaffold-independent reactions kinetically distinct. Beta-catenin phosphorylation creates beta-TrCP recognition motif leading to ubiquitination and degradation. Wnt signals disrupt complex geometry without inhibiting GSK3B directly. APC truncation (>80% CRC) prevents destruction complex assembly despite normal GSK3B. In insulin/PI3K-Akt pathway, Akt phosphorylates GSK3B Ser9 causing ~200-fold inhibition, relieving inhibition of glycogen synthase and eIF2B, promoting glycogen/protein synthesis. In cell cycle/proliferation, GSK3B phosphorylates c-Myc (Thr58), cyclin D1 (Thr286), creating phosphodegrons for FBW7-mediated degradation. In neurodegeneration, GSK3B hyperphosphorylates tau at >40 sites reducing microtubule binding and promoting aggregation. Priming requirement (P+4 phosphate recognized by R96-R180-K205 pocket) provides substrate specificity and enables processivity (sequential C-to-N phosphorylation). Constitutive pTyr216 autophosphorylation maintains basal activity. GSK3B is signaling hub integrating Wnt, insulin, growth factor, and stress pathways.

disease_associations.description: GSK3B intronic polymorphism IVS2-68G>A significantly associated with AD (14.6% in AD patients, 10.8% in FTD patients vs 4.1% in controls; p<0.01). GSK3B is major tau kinase; hyperactivity leads to hyperphosphorylation at Thr231, Ser235, Ser396, Ser404 and >40 other sites producing hyperphosphorylated tau that detaches from microtubules and aggregates into paired helical filaments forming neurofibrillary tangles, pathological hallmark of AD. GSK3B also implicated in amyloid plaques via APP processing. GSK3B genetic variants associated with CSF biomarkers total-tau and Aβ42. Prime therapeutic target; lithium and other GSK3 inhibitors show promise in AD models.

GSK3B dysregulation central to insulin resistance. Constitutive GSK3B activity phosphorylates and inactivates glycogen synthase (Ser640/644/648/652), impairing glycogen synthesis despite insulin signaling. GSK3B also phosphorylates IRS1 on serine residues creating negative feedback loop that impairs insulin receptor signaling. Elevated GSK3B expression/activity in skeletal muscle of T2D patients. Insulin resistance can result from impaired Akt-mediated Ser9 phosphorylation of GSK3B. Target for insulin sensitizers and diabetes therapeutics; GSK3 inhibition improves glucose homeostasis in models.

disease_associations.mutation_type: Somatic mutations in APC/CTNNB1 (not GSK3B itself)
disease_associations.description: APC truncation mutations occur in >80% of colorectal cancers, predominantly in mutation cluster region that eliminates beta-catenin binding repeats and AXIN binding sites. Despite normal GSK3B expression and activity, APC loss prevents destruction complex assembly, blocking GSK3B-mediated beta-catenin phosphorylation and degradation. Less commonly (~10% CRC), activating CTNNB1 mutations at Ser33, Ser37, Thr41, or Ser45 prevent GSK3B/CK1 phosphorylation. Both mechanisms cause beta-catenin accumulation driving constitutive Wnt pathway activation and tumorigenesis. Demonstrates absolute dependence on scaffold (AXIN/APC) for GSK3B function toward beta-catenin; free GSK3B essentially inactive. Highlights difference between enzyme activity and effective pathway output.

GSK3B is direct pharmacological target of lithium therapy for bipolar disorder. Lithium inhibits GSK3B activity (IC50 ~2 mM therapeutic range) through competition with Mg2+ and affecting Ser9 phosphorylation. Lithium's mood-stabilizing effects attributed largely to GSK3B inhibition affecting neurotransmitter signaling, circadian rhythms (via CLOCK/BMAL1 phosphorylation), neuroplasticity, and neuroprotection. Genetic association studies have reported GSK3B variants linked to bipolar disorder susceptibility and lithium response.

GSK3B promoter SNP rs334558 influences transcriptional activity and associated with grey matter volume differences in schizophrenia patients. Post-mortem studies show GSK3β protein levels 41% lower in prefrontal cortex of schizophrenic patients vs controls, indicating abnormal GSK3 regulation plays role in pathophysiology. GSK3B involved in neurodevelopment, synaptic plasticity, and dopamine signaling relevant to schizophrenia.

GSK3β contributes to genesis and maintenance of neurodegenerative changes in PD. Involved in alpha-synuclein phosphorylation and aggregation. Contributes to dopaminergic neuron degeneration. GSK3 inhibition shows neuroprotective effects in PD models.

Role context-dependent. In Wnt-driven cancers, GSK3B inhibition (via APC/CTNNB1 mutations, autocrine Wnt) drives tumorigenesis. In other contexts, GSK3B can be oncogenic or tumor suppressive. Phosphorylates and destabilizes c-Myc, cyclin D1 (tumor suppressor function). In some cancers, GSK3B promotes survival, invasion, drug resistance (oncogenic function). Context-specificity limits therapeutic targeting.

metadata.data_quality_notes: Exceptionally high quality data. Kinase domain extensively characterized with >140 PDB structures including ATP-bound (1PYX, 2.4Å), primed substrate-bound (1GNG showing phosphate binding pocket), and highest-resolution apo form (1J1B, 1.8Å showing constitutively active conformation). Post-translational modifications comprehensively characterized: Ser9 and Tyr216 sites have extensive biochemical validation with mechanistic understanding. Quantitative kinetic parameters from landmark study (Gavagan et al. 2023 eLife, doi:10.7554/eLife.85444, PMID:36594429) provide detailed KM values: 0.27 µM for GSK3B:AXIN:pS45-beta-catenin complex vs ≥2 µM for pS9-GSK3B or free GSK3B, demonstrating >20,000-fold scaffold enhancement - one of most dramatic scaffold effects in cell signaling. AXIN binding interface structurally characterized (hydrophobic channel residues 260-300). Substrate specificity (P+4 priming via R96-R180-K205 pocket) unique to GSK3 and well-understood structurally and mechanistically. Destruction complex mechanism extensively studied. Priming requirement, processivity, and sequential two-kinase mechanism (CK1→GSK3B) well-established. Some limitations: isoform 2 full sequence not in databases; specific acetylation/ubiquitination/nitrosylation sites need residue-level detail; tissue-specific splice variants and regulatory mechanisms partially characterized. AlphaFold complements experimental structures for disordered C-terminal region. Excellent resource for quantitative pathway modeling.
metadata.modeling_relevance_summary: GSK3B is quintessential example of scaffold-dependent enzyme and regulatory node in Wnt signaling controlling beta-catenin stability. CRITICAL MODELING FEATURES: (1) Priming requirement (P+4 phosphate recognized by R96-R180-K205) creates substrate specificity and sequential phosphorylation logic - MUST represent in reaction rules; (2) AXIN scaffold enhancement (>20,000-fold) makes scaffold-dependent vs scaffold-independent states kinetically distinct - free GSK3B essentially inactive toward beta-catenin (KM >2 µM no saturation) vs GSK3B:AXIN complex highly active (KM=0.27 µM); this is NOT incremental enhancement but conversion of inactive to active enzyme-substrate pair; (3) Ser9 phosphorylation by Akt provides insulin/growth factor input with ~200-fold inhibition via pseudo-substrate mechanism blocking priming pocket; AXIN partially protects (7-fold decrease in Ser9 phosphorylation efficiency); (4) Tyr216 autophosphorylation required for basal activity (~5-fold), constitutive in cells, Y216F nearly abolishes activity; (5) Processivity: after CK1 primes Ser45, GSK3B sequentially phosphorylates Thr41→Ser37→Ser33 (C-to-N direction); each phosphorylation primes next; (6) Two-kinase sequential mechanism: CK1α primes Ser45 (>1000-fold effect), then GSK3B acts; (7) AXIN rate-limiting: cellular AXIN ~1000-fold lower than GSK3B/beta-catenin/APC making AXIN concentration critical parameter; (8) APC truncation phenotype: loss of scaffold despite normal GSK3B completely prevents beta-catenin degradation - demonstrates scaffold is obligate component, not enhancer; models MUST include scaffold binding explicitly; (9) Wnt mechanism: DVL recruitment disrupts complex geometry/substrate access without inhibiting GSK3B directly; (10) Quantitative parameters available for implementation: KM=0.27 µM (AXIN-bound), >20,000-fold scaffold effect, ~200-fold Ser9 inhibition, ~5-fold pY216 activation. Essential for modeling APC tumor suppressor loss, Wnt pathway dynamics, insulin regulation of metabolism, beta-catenin-TCF transcription, tau phosphorylation in neurodegeneration. Paradigm for understanding how scaffolds convert weak enzyme-substrate interactions into efficient catalytic systems.
